patterns.key_values: marketing key-art hero (web/brand, 1200x630 OG-card ratio): single centered wordmark on a drenched sky-blue vertical gradient (#8ACBEC top -> #CFE9F3 horizon), white paper plane below with a torn-notebook-tab seam ascending L->R, two halftone clouds; screenprint dot grain throughout. No app UI, no CTA, no device frame.

signature_moves: Riso-print sky poster: ben-day halftone screenprint grain + drenched sky-blue + a bold rounded-deco wordmark puts a printed-poster register on a digital notes app — the entire memorable budget spent on texture + bespoke letterforms, not on a product shot

Scene-as-pitch (subject-mining): the composition literally stages the concept — an open sky of 'big ideas' meeting a white page along a torn-notebook seam of ascending paper tabs; a built scene from the product's own materials (paper/notebook/sky), not a generic gradient backdrop

Bespoke geometric-rounded wordmark: CRAFT set in a custom single-story deco display (circular bowls, flat cuts) so brand identity rides entirely on the letterforms; the near-black ink is the one Von-Restorff pop on a pale field
defects: No true design defect observable on the poster itself — it is competent, committed key-art

Corpus-input gap (NOT an app defect): the submission ships ONLY a brand key-art cover + a 256px icon. This is thinner than a typical marketing composite — no product window, no lockup, not even a CTA — so it yields essentially zero product-design evidence

aesthetic.direction: Riso-print playful-poster (screenprint brand key-art): remixes the range map's Playful/toy display type (chunky rounded-geometric) with an Organic/soft grain texture over a near-drenched sky-blue + white-paper + black palette. A committed, subject-mined direction — clearly authored, not template-default
aesthetic.cluster_hint: riso-print-brand-poster (web/marketing surface, NOT a macOS-UI cluster)

psychology: First-impression / 50ms thesis (Lindgaard) — the sky + rounded wordmark reads 'open, imaginative, friendly' pre-cognitively; the hero is a mood statement, correct job for an OG key-art card
Von Restorff / signal-detection — exactly one saturated-dark element (the black wordmark) on an otherwise pale-blue field makes it the unmissable focal point

Processing fluency / aesthetic-usability (Reber; Kurosu & Kashimura) — a tightly limited palette (sky-blue, white, black) plus high-craft print texture buys the perceived-quality/trust halo on first contact
Subject-mining (practitioner) — building the scene from the product's own materials (paper, notebook, sky) makes the imagery specific and ownable rather than a stock gradient
